newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end fraction higher in thin market.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end fraction higher in thin market.

text.p: French shares ended steady on Friday, above the psychologically important 2,300 level, supported by a firm, if tired, Wall Street, traders said.

Paris nudged higher after bond markets welcomed U.S. durable goods orders which came in down 1.6 percent and weaker-than- forecast jobless claims of 335,000. But reaction here was subdued. "The market yawned and turned over," said one broker.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 3.20 points or 0.14 percent at 2,306.95. The index was up 1.24 percent on the week.
The CAC-40 futures contract was up 1.5 at 2,305.5 on Thursday's close.
Volume, including foreign shares, was 2.9 billion francs.
Retailer Carrefour, a favourite blue chip among foreign investors, gains 0.68 percent to 3,400 francs.
Luxury goods group LVMH, another stock of choice for non-domestics, rises 2.16 percent to 1,422 francs, helped by hopes of purchase of the renowned Chateau d'Yquem vineyard.
Sports goods company Salomon, helped by strong snowfalls which are expected to help sales of skis, firms 2.76 percent to 446.
Sugar gaint Saint-Louis stages catch-up after lagging the market, adds 2.34 percent to 1,270.
Tobacco group Seita falls 0.92 percent to 215, off lows, battered by a second French cancer victim lawsuit.
